technologies.how: Interpreted modules, asyncio, dataclasses, typing, subprocess adapters, and scientific libraries.
technologies.name: Python
technologies.what: Rapidly composes AI, automation, analysis, and control-plane workflows.
technologies.when: Use when iteration speed, ecosystem breadth, and readable coordination dominate the boundary.
technologies.where: Mission orchestration, model tooling, document pipelines, tests, and integration glue.
technologies.why: It offers the strongest general AI ecosystem and the lowest friction for composing heterogeneous systems.

technologies.how: Goroutines, channels, contexts, interfaces, and binary/network packages.
technologies.name: Go
technologies.what: Builds simple, deployable concurrent network services and telemetry processors.
technologies.when: Use when many I/O-bound tasks need straightforward concurrency and operational simplicity.
technologies.where: Gateways, control-plane daemons, streaming telemetry, and cloud infrastructure.
technologies.why: Goroutines, channels, static binaries, and a disciplined standard library reduce service complexity.

technologies.how: Structural typing, discriminated unions, async/await, streams, and Node/browser APIs.
technologies.name: TypeScript
technologies.what: Adds static contracts to JavaScript's browser, Node.js, and event-driven ecosystem.
technologies.when: Use when the boundary is web-native, JSON/RPC-heavy, or shared between frontend and backend.
technologies.where: MCP gateways, web applications, browser agents, connectors, and asynchronous control surfaces.
technologies.why: It catches interface drift before runtime while retaining JavaScript's deployment reach.

technologies.how: Classes, interfaces, ExecutorService, blocking queues, records, and the JVM memory model.
technologies.name: Java
technologies.what: Owns the JVM runtime baseline for enterprise services, Android, and portable bytecode deployment.
technologies.when: Use when the operational contract is the JVM itself and long-lived enterprise ecosystems matter.
technologies.where: Application servers, batch gateways, Android runtimes, and cross-organization service boundaries.
technologies.why: Java remains the universal JVM ABI and the language other JVM languages must interoperate with.

technologies.how: Null-safety, data classes, coroutines-style structured concurrency, and multiplatform source sets.
technologies.name: Kotlin
technologies.what: Modern JVM and multiplatform language with null-safety and structured concurrency.
technologies.when: Use when new JVM work needs safer defaults, concise syntax, and optional multiplatform reach.
technologies.where: Android, server services, shared business logic, and agent runtimes on the JVM.
technologies.why: It is the practical successor language for most new JVM development while preserving full Java interop.

technologies.how: Value semantics, protocols, async/await, ARC, SIMD, and Metal APIs.
technologies.name: Swift
technologies.what: Builds safe native software for Apple platforms and interoperates with Metal.
technologies.when: Use when the target is Apple's runtime, UI stack, or GPU/ANE ecosystem.
technologies.where: macOS/iOS applications, Apple Silicon inference, Metal compute, and device-native interfaces.
technologies.why: It combines native performance, safety features, and first-class Apple framework access.

technologies.how: Processes, mailboxes, pattern matching, GenServer, supervisors, and OTP releases.
technologies.name: Elixir
technologies.what: Runs massive numbers of isolated processes under supervision on the BEAM.
technologies.when: Use when fault isolation, uptime, and highly concurrent messaging dominate.
technologies.where: Realtime backends, event systems, self-healing clusters, and coordination services.
technologies.why: BEAM supervision and actor semantics make failure a managed lifecycle event.

technologies.how: Algebraic data types, pattern matching, type classes, monads, and laziness.
technologies.name: Haskell
technologies.what: Expresses pure transformations and rich type-level models with controlled effects.
technologies.when: Use when algebraic structure and purity simplify reasoning about complex state.
technologies.where: Compilers, DSLs, formal models, financial logic, and correctness-sensitive transformations.
technologies.why: Its type system and immutable semantics make invalid transformations harder to express.
